<section class="home-about" aria-labelledby="about-heading">
<div class="section-command" id="about-heading"><span>$</span> about</div>

<p><a href="research.qmd">My research</a> develops and applies methods in causal inference, decision modeling, and reinforcement learning to generate and synthesize evidence for better decision-making in health and public policy. I study the impacts of physician behavior, health policies, and personalized medicine.</p>

<p>I am an NIMH T32 Predoctoral Research Fellow in Comparative Effectiveness Research for Suicide Prevention at <a href="https://www.brighamandwomens.org">Brigham and Women’s Hospital</a> and a Research Statistician with the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs.</p>

<p>I also care deeply about <a href="teaching.qmd">teaching</a>. I have been fortunate to work with students at Harvard, the University of Chicago, and New Haven Public Schools during my time as a Teach For America corps member.</p>

<div class="research-topics" aria-label="Research areas">
<span>causal inference</span>
<span>decision modeling</span>
<span>reinforcement learning</span>
<span>health policy</span>
</div>
